data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: ticket
sections.question: ticket
sections.summary: a small piece of paper or card that shows you have paid to travel or enter somewhere

senses.definition: a small piece of paper or card that shows you have paid to travel on a form of transport or to enter a place such as a cinema or concert
examples: She bought a ticket for the train to London at the station.
He lost his ticket and could not get into the concert.

answers.answer: She bought a ticket for the train to London at the station.
He drank a hot ticket at the café before boarding the bus.
She cooked a ticket in the pan and served it for dinner.
They planted tickets in the garden and watered them every morning.

sections.title: train
sections.question: train
sections.summary: a vehicle that travels along railway tracks; also to teach someone a skill through practice

senses.definition: a long vehicle that travels along railway tracks, with an engine pulling a series of carriages carrying passengers or goods
examples: He took the train to work because the buses were on strike.
The train arrived at the platform ten minutes late.

senses.definition: to teach someone the skills they need for a particular job or activity, especially through repeated practice
examples: She is training to become a nurse at the local hospital.
He trains at the gym three times a week to prepare for the race.

answers.answer: He took the train to work because the buses were on strike.
She cooked the train for dinner and served it with vegetables.
He planted a train in his garden to grow food for the winter.
She drank a cold train after her run in the park.
